EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.

Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: The Northpeak and Kaggle bullets appear to list the same futures signal achievement under two different entries.
items.because: Both describe an order-book imbalance signal tested over 18 months, with equivalent Sharpe increases.

items.says: Sunrise Bakery leads the experience section with work unrelated to the résumé’s quantitative focus.
items.because: The bakery role shapes the reader’s initial impression and takes space that could foreground more relevant experience.

items.says: The weekly labour budget result gives no figure.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether costs were meaningfully under budget or how consistent the result was.

items.says: “Managed” is past tense even though this is a current role.
items.because: Past tense makes an ongoing responsibility sound completed.

items.says: “Ran” is past tense even though this is a current role.
items.because: Past tense makes an ongoing responsibility sound completed.

items.says: The reduction in unsold bread is attributed to counts and orders without explaining how they changed decisions.
items.because: The bullet does not establish that link, and demand changes or other factors could explain the reduction.

items.says: “Risk-adjusted returns by 35%” does not name the metric or its comparison.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what measure changed or what baseline the 35% uses.

items.says: Purged walk-forward splits and an embargo do not guarantee that every decision used only information available at the time.
items.because: Future information can still enter through timestamps, revisions, features or execution assumptions.

items.says: “Validated the signal” does not say what the validation found.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether the signal held up or what conclusion the test supported.

items.says: The best Sharpe among 400 backtested configurations is not an expected live Sharpe.
items.because: Selecting the strongest result tends to inflate its measured Sharpe and does not establish live performance.

items.says: Two Northpeak bullets appear to claim roughly the same improvement in the futures book’s risk-adjusted performance.
items.because: A reader may not know whether the 35% improvement and the Sharpe rise from 1.1 to 1.5 are separate results.

items.says: Using the same random seed on every worker does not establish 2,000 independent Monte Carlo trials.
items.because: Workers with the same seed and generator can produce identical random-number sequences.

items.says: “My proof” uses a first-person pronoun and splits the result across clauses.
items.because: The phrasing shifts attention away from the tightened bound and makes the result less direct.

items.says: The stated tests across 30 indices do not establish significance within both crisis periods.
items.because: A full-sample test does not establish significance within a crisis-period subsample.

items.says: The competition modeling bullet gives no result from the work.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether the modeling improved prediction or contributed to the competition.

items.says: “For a market prediction competition” repeats the project title.
items.because: The repeated context uses space without adding information.

items.says: The score change does not establish that the new folds reduced leakage or caused the gap to close.
items.because: Leaderboard gaps can also arise from distribution shift, noise or other evaluation differences.

items.says: Kafka is listed without supporting experience elsewhere in the résumé.
items.because: A reader cannot see where it was used or assess the depth of experience with it.
The visible spelling error can make the skills section look insufficiently checked.
